item.title: Fallacies of AI
item.description:
The Fallacies of LLMs

Inspired by The Fallacies of Distributed Computing, here are common misconceptions about Large Language Models (LLMs):

1. The model knows facts.

LLMs don’t “know” — they generate plausible text based on training patterns. Correctness is not guaranteed.

2. Bigger models always mean better results.

Scale helps, but alignment, fine-tuning, prompting, and context management matter just as much.

3. The model understands like a human.

LLMs simulate reasoning through prediction, not genuine comprehension or intention.
